## General info

Code used for creating long-billed hermit song cultural evolution trees and analyzing evolutionary patterns.

## Song segmenting

Songs are now coded as sequences of 5 ms segments with 5 possible states, in four steps. The [full report](https://marce10.github.io/lbh_cultural_evolution_revBayes/scripts/song_segment_coding.html) is built from `scripts/song_segment_coding.qmd`. Measurements use dominant frequency contours extracted with warbleR's `freq_ts()` and manually tailored where needed.

1. **Manual broad sections**: each song is divided into pure tone and trill sections. Consecutive pure tone sections are merged, and trills that differ discretely in rate stay as separate sections
2. **Classify trills**: each whole trill section is fast (F, period < 13 ms) or slow (S, period ≥ 13 ms)
3. **Split into 5 ms segments**: the whole song is split, and trill segments take the state of their section
4. **Classify pure tones**: each tone segment is descending (D, slope < -14 kHz/s), flat (P) or ascending (U, slope ≥ 14 kHz/s), with the slope measured in a 15 ms window

Output files are in `data/processed`:

| Output | Five leks used in the paper (197 recordings, 104 song types) | All leks (322 recordings, 187 song types) |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| Segments | `song_segments_by_recording.csv` | `song_segments_by_recording_all_leks.csv` |
| Sequence per song type and year | `song_sequences_by_taxon.csv` | `song_sequences_by_taxon_all_leks.csv` |
| One sequence per song type | `song_sequences_by_song_type.csv` | `song_sequences_by_song_type_all_leks.csv` |
| FASTA of all recordings | `song_sequences/all_recordings.fa` | `song_sequences/all_recordings_all_leks.fa` |
| FASTA files for alignment | `song_sequences/song_type_sequence/` and `song_sequences/year_specific_sequence/` | not available |

## Song alignment

The songs of the five leks in the paper are aligned using one sequence per song type (`song_sequences/song_type_sequence/`), as in the first version of the study. The [full report](https://marce10.github.io/lbh_cultural_evolution_revBayes/scripts/song_alignment.html) is built from `scripts/song_alignment.qmd`.

There are three alignment strategies:

| Strategy | File name | Method |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| MAFFT-optimal | `optimal` | MAFFT L-INS-i with optimized scores: -2 (different category), -0.75 (same category), 2 (same state) |
| MAFFT-agnostic | `agnostic` | MAFFT L-INS-i with the same score for any mismatch: 1 (mismatch), 1.5 (same state) |
| PRANK | `prank` | The most central alignment among 100 seeds |

Each song type is aligned once, and the datasets are built from that alignment, so `all` and `bounds` have identical aligned rows:

Datasets combine the years of each song type (`all` or `bounds`) with the historical records used (`full`, `recent` or `none`):

| Dataset | Songs included | Leks | Nexus files (× 3 strategies) | RevBayes models (× 2 clocks) |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|-----:|-----:|
| `all_recent` | All years, recordings after 2000 | BR1, CCE, HC1, SUR, TR1 | 15 | 30 |
| `bounds_recent` | First and last year of each song type, recordings after 2000 | BR1, CCE, HC1, SUR, TR1 | 15 | 30 |
| `all_full` | All years, including recordings before 2000 | CCE, HC1, SUR | 9 | 18 |
| `bounds_full` | First and last year of each song type, including recordings before 2000 | CCE, HC1, SUR | 9 | 18 |
| `none` | Song types in the last year of sampling (no historical records) | BR1, SUR, TR1 | 9 | 18 |
| **Total** | | | **57** | **114** |

The historical records were named `new` (now `recent`), `old` (now `full`) and `no.fossils` (now `none`) in the first version of the study. Files named `early` (only the first year of each song type) are base alignments and are not analyzed.

`bounds` replaces `early` from the first version of the study. `early` misses song types that persist until the last year of sampling, which conflicts with assuming that all songs in that year were sampled (rho = 1), so it is now used only as the base alignment.

Output files and scripts:

| Output | Location | Script |
|:-----|:-----|:-----|
| Nexus files for RevBayes: `<lek>_<strategy>_<dataset>_alignment.nex` | `data/processed/nexus/` | `scripts/write_nexus.R` |
| Taxon files for RevBayes (columns `taxon` and `age`, in years before the last year of sampling): `<lek>_<dataset>_taxa.tsv`, the same for the three strategies | `data/processed/taxa/` | `scripts/write_nexus.R` |
| Alignments, scoring matrices and results | `data/processed/alignments/` | `scripts/align_song_types.R` |
| PRANK runs and selection | `data/processed/alignments/prank_seeds/` | `scripts/prank_seeds.R` |
| MAFFT score optimization | `data/processed/mafft_optimization/` | `scripts/optimize_mafft_costs.R` |

## Next steps

The analyses below were run on the earlier sequences (`segments_by_song_type.csv`, 20 segments, 6 states) and **need to be redone** with the new 5 ms, 5-state sequences, in this order.

**Sequences and alignments**

- [x] Choose the FASTA version for the alignments: `song_type_sequence`, as in the first version of the study
- [x] Redo the MAFFT cost optimization for the 5 states
- [x] Rerun the MAFFT and PRANK alignments, and check gaps and convergence
- [x] Replace `early` with `bounds` and write the nexus files (`data/processed/nexus/`)

**RevBayes**

- [ ] Write the `.Rev` scripts of the 114 models from `scripts/template.Rev` (`scripts/trees_with_revbayes.Rmd`), pointing to `data/processed/nexus/` and `data/processed/taxa/` with the new file names (e.g. `BR1_optimal_bounds_recent_alignment.nex` and `BR1_bounds_recent_taxa.tsv`). The scripts of the first version are in `archive/scripts/`
- [ ] Update the base RevBayes files for RevBayes 1.4.2: `dnFBDP` instead of `dnFBDRP` in `scripts/model_FBDP.Rev`, and taxon files with an `age` column (as in `scripts/revbayes_beast2_comparison/`)
- [ ] Change the GTR model from 6 to 5 states, which means 5 stationary frequencies and 10 exchangeability rates (`scripts/model_GTRG.Rev`, `scripts/none/model_GTRG_BD.Rev`)
- [ ] Confirm that rho = 1 and the treatment of gaps still fit the new data (about half of each alignment is gaps)
- [ ] Rerun all 114 models (`scripts/trees_with_revbayes.Rmd`), including those with no historical records (`none`)
- [ ] Rerun the posterior predictions (P3; `scripts/Write_P3.Rmd`, `scripts/run_P3_*.sh`)

**Results**

- [ ] Redo the MCMC, ML and P3 diagnostics (`archive/scripts/Model diagnostics.Rmd`, `archive/scripts/rwty_diagnostics.Rmd`)
- [ ] Redo the tree topology diagnostics (`archive/scripts/tree_topology_diagnostics_oct_2024.qmd`)
- [ ] Redo the descriptive statistics (`archive/scripts/descriptive_stats.Rmd`)
- [ ] Redo the regression models (`archive/scripts/regression_models.qmd`, `archive/scripts/song_sequence_similarity.qmd`)
- [ ] Assess the effect of the redundancy of 5 ms sequences (neighbouring segments mostly repeat the same state) on the trees
- [ ] Check which results depend on the alignment strategy, and interpret results found only with PRANK with care, especially in BR1, SUR and the `full` datasets, where PRANK alignments vary among seeds

**Manuscript**

- [ ] Rewrite the methods on sound classification and song coding (now 5 ms segments and 5 states instead of 20 segments and 6 categories), including Fig. 2
- [ ] Update the methods on alignment: new MAFFT scores and how they were selected, PRANK selection among seeds (both rules were set after inspecting the results), later years taking the aligned row of their song type, MAFFT convergence, and `bounds` instead of `early`
- [ ] Correct the leks in the analyses with no fossils: the text says "3 or more distinct songs" in the last year, but the code uses more than 3, which excludes HC1 (exactly 3)
- [ ] Replace the repeatability results with the agreement between copies of the same song type, and update the supplementary text (`archive/scripts/segment_classification_repeatability.qmd`)

## Repository structure

Only the files needed to reproduce the current analyses, and to run the RevBayes models, are kept in `scripts/`, `data/` and `output/`:

| Folder | Contents |
|:-----|:-----|
| `scripts/` | 5 ms coding, alignment and nexus scripts and reports, the RevBayes and BEAST2 comparison (`revbayes_beast2_comparison/`), and the base RevBayes files (models, MCMC, marginal likelihood and P3; `none/` for the models without historical records) |
| `data/raw/` | Raw data (segment classification and the years in which each song type was recorded) |
| `data/processed/` | 5 ms sequences, alignments, nexus and taxon files, and the sampling years per lek (`sampling_years_by_lek.csv`) |
| `output/` | Results of the RevBayes and BEAST2 comparison (`revbayes_beast2_comparison/`) and figures |
| `archive/` | Scripts, data and results of the first version of the study (20 segments and 6 states), kept with the same folder structure |

## Website

The website is built with Quarto (`_quarto.yml`, `index.qmd`) and deployed to GitHub Pages by `.github/workflows/publish.yml` on each push to `master`. Code results are read from `_freeze/`, so after editing a report run `quarto render` and commit `_freeze/`.
